content: Hi Guys, it seems today this paper was uploaded on Arxiv in order to disprove the claim that Lean certificate of NS actually works. Do you have any thought on this? Ad far as I know the main statement was formalized by the Lean community right? So at least the main statement should hold https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08144
I think this is a well known thing that the formalization of an AI natural language proof doesn’t always match the original natural language and may even fix errors.

I was talking about something similar with @David Roe recently. He suggested when formalizing a textbook or paper we may want two things:

  • A formalization of the main results which fits Lean/Mathlib/Tau Ceti well
  • Additional Lean theorems which match every definition/theorem/lemma in the book/paper verbatim. These may just be links to the above Lean code, or they may be specializations or restatements of how things are presented in the lean code.

This provides better semantic alignment to the source material without compromising good Lean style.

Now in cases like NS and the OpenAI drop, in the future we may similarly ask/require that the natural language write ups be rewritten so that every lemma is supported by Lean, even providing blueprint style links back to the Lean code. But again as the models get better at writing both good Lean and good natural language math, we probably don’t want the natural language to be a verbatim translation of the Lean, hence the need for this intermediate linking layer of Lean code.

Jason Rute said:

I think this is a well known thing that the formalization of an AI natural language proof doesn’t always match the original natural language and may even fix errors.

Yes, this was also my impression, even human made verification don’t always encode the proof exactly like the “informal” one. I’m wondering what that paper want to show. Is it their way to invalidate the Lean certificate? Maybe I’m missing a layer here

This was discussed in #general > Lean in the wild: Navier-Stokes proved @ 💬 .

In the case of NS, agents found issues and corrected them during formalization, but the corrections and "diverging proof methods" are not reflected in the informal proof.
And also importantly in #general > Independent verification of OpenAI NavierStokesAndEuler

But to summarize where NS is: I’ve seen a number of people here say that the Lean proof of NS seems correct. The statement is correct (and matches the independent formalization by Google DeepMind), and the code compiles even with the new verified checkers. I’ve also seen people say that the natural language NS paper is really badly written and hard to follow (and some have even commented previously on the mismatch between the Lean and the paper).
